hook.line: Someone always trips in the café, and the first question is whether they are all right. Spanish has an everyday way to say who fell and what hurts.
hook.es: Se cayó de la bicicleta, pero no se lastimó.
hook.en: She fell off her bike, but she didn't get hurt.

examples.es: Se cayó de la bicicleta, pero no se lastimó.
examples.en: She fell off her bike, but she didn't get hurt.

examples.es: Me hice daño en la rodilla.
Vale se cayó de la silla.

examples.en: Did you hurt yourself? (to a friend)

rule:
*Caerse* is falling by accident. After it, *de* says what from (*de la silla*), *en* says where (*en la calle*), *por* says down or through (*por la escalera*).
To say you got hurt, *lastimarse* is the everyday choice in Latin America; *hacerse daño* works everywhere. For the body part, *en* with *hacerse daño*: *me hice daño en la rodilla*. With *golpearse* and *lastimarse* it follows directly: *me golpeé la cabeza*.
Body parts take *la*, not *mi*.
smallPrint: Teachers call these reflexive verbs. Plain *caer*, without *se*, is for rain, prices or dates falling.

readAndPick.es: Se cayó de la bicicleta, pero no se lastimó.
options: She fell off her bike and got hurt.
She fell off her bike, but she didn't get hurt.

options: I'm going to hurt my knee.

readAndPick.es: Vale se cayó de la silla.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Vale ___ cayó de la silla.* (*se* or *me*) Vale fell off the chair.
yourTurn.answer: Vale se cayó de la silla.
yourTurn.why: Vale is a third person, so *se*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Me golpeé ___ cabeza.* (*la* or *mi*) I hit my head.
yourTurn.why: Body parts take *la*, because *me* already says whose.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: I fell down the stairs.
yourTurn.why: Falling is *caerse*, so *me caí*, with *por* for down.

yourTurn.prompt: Ask a friend: Did you hurt yourself?

accept: Me hice daño en la espalda.
yourTurn.why: *Me lastimé* then the body part with *la*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about Tomás: *Me golpeé la mano.*

pitfalls.why: Almost. The *me* already says whose head, so use *la*.

pitfalls.right: Vale se cayó de la silla.
pitfalls.why: Falling by accident is *caerse*, so it needs *se*.

pitfalls.right: Me hice daño en la rodilla.
pitfalls.why: With *hacerse daño*, the body part needs *en* and an article.

personal: Think of a time you fell or hurt yourself: a bike, stairs, ice, a football match. Write what happened with *me caí…* and what hurt with *me lastimé…* or *me golpeé…*.
